notes.title: Train World Update — Coupling & Uncoupling Arrives!
notes.notes:
A major new gameplay feature is here: manual wagon coupling and uncoupling! This update brings deeper control, new waypoint tools, new locomotives, and dozens of improvements and fixes.
[h2]🔩 New Features & Mechanics[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Coupling and Uncoupling of Wagons[/b] - trains can now uncouple and re-couple wagons at designated waypoints. Coupling is only possible with wagons that were previously uncoupled. Includes new sounds, a tutorial, and error handling for uncoupled locomotives.
[*] [b]Trains Without Wagons or Locomotives Remain on Tracks[/b] - wagons without locomotives stay on the  rails, and locomotive-only trains can move independently
[*] [b]Movement in Reverse[/b] - available at waypoints where a train changes direction (signals and passenger stations). Enables more advanced route setups.
[*] [b]Coupling & Uncoupling Tutorial[/b] - a step-by-step guide that walks players through how to manage this new mechanic.
[/list]
[h2]🚦 Waypoint System Updates[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Priority Load[/b] - when enabled, a train will prioritize loading cargo/passengers specifically for the selected connection.
[*] [b]Wait for Full Train[/b] - train waits until fully loaded (based on selected percentage or amount) with any available cargo/passengers.
[*] [b]Waypoint UI[/b] - updated Waypoint Settings Interface and new icons for active options like “Full train”. Now waypoint settings can be edited without entering route edit mode
[/list]
[h2]🚆 New Locomotives[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]0-8-0 USRA[/b] (2nd Era Steam)
[*] [b]SDP40F[/b] (3rd Era Diesel)
[/list]
[h2]⚙️ Gameplay Improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] Updated steam engine stats (power, speed, and price now reflect historical data)
[*] Adjusted one-time contract cargo amounts and rewards
[*] Population growth tuning (affects production)
[*] Adjusted production rates for Aluminum and Machines industries
[*] Optimized CPU and memory usage in train simulation
[*] Large train list display performance significantly improved
[*] Added UI scaling setting
[/list]
[h2]🎨 Visual & UI Updates[/h2]
[list]
[*] Updated loading screen backgrounds
[*] Updated brick tunnel entrance model
[*] Fixed missing shadows in cities
[*] Adjusted shadow distance parameters
[*] Updated general UI style
[*] Time labels added to “Full Load” and “Wait for Connection”
[*] Labels added to the age graph in "Replace" and "Inventory" panels
[/list]
[h2]🧰 Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Resolved issue with trains getting stuck at stations with specific waypoint configurations
[*] Fixed “Mastering the Research Tree” tutorial
[*] Resolved game hang on failed save file load
[*] Fixed train stopping abruptly at signals
[*] Train jumping when editing active routes
[*] Trains no longer stop on signal waypoints when load conditions are already met
[*] Incorrect cargo/passenger display after removing trains
[*] Fixed long locomotives hanging off rails
[*] Fixed display issues with stations, depots, signals, and contract connections
[*] Corrected one-time contract cargo amount display
[*] Resolved incorrect wait time calculations for full train/connection options
[*] Max wait time for auto-wait and full load set to 90 minutes
[*] Resolved flipped values in the “Targets and Statistics” panel
[*] Fixed game freezing on save files with corrupted rails
[*] Train display and payments are now correctly handled
[*] Fixed UI waypoint button error
[*] Fixed freight priority logic
[*] Fixed rail placement for locomotives
[*] Trains now properly resume movement after signal wait with fulfilled load condition
[*] Various language fixes
[/list]
🛤️ This first implementation of wagon coupling/uncoupling lays the foundation for more interesting features. Stay tuned for future updates!

💬 Let me know how you’re using coupling in your networks!
Your feedback drives development — join the conversation and share your creations.

notes.title: 🚂 Silverstream Update & More! 🌟
notes.notes:
[h2]Hello, Train World community![/h2]
I’m thrilled to share some exciting updates and improvements we’ve made recently. These changes are designed to enhance your gameplay experience and add new depth to the world of Train World. Let’s dive into what’s new!
[h3]🌍New Content:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Silverstream Bay Map:[/b] Explore this charming new map featuring a central shipping lane, picturesque mountain ranges, and a flowing river.
[/list][h3]🛠️Gameplay Enhancements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Wagons Panel:[/b] Easily view available cargo types and compatible wagons with the new Wagons panel, accessible next to the "Help" button.
[*] [b]Prestige Mechanic: [/b]Keep track of your Prestige, which grows through activities like purchasing trains, unlocking regions, and more. Prestige decay ensures active gameplay, adding a new layer of strategy.
[/list][h3]🎯 Map Targets and Achievements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Complete map targets with achievements to "win" the map and earn stars based on the difficulty level.
[/list][h3]🌅 Visual & UI Improvements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Dynamic Daylight: [/b]Enjoy beautiful daylight color changes based on the sun’s angle.
[*] [b]Enhanced Minimap: [/b]Navigate with ease thanks to color-coded rails, optimized icon sizes, and new icons for village production.
[/list][h3]⚖️ Balancing Adjustments:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Loans & Region Prices:[/b] I’ve fine-tuned loan rates and region prices, with adjustments based on the number of regions you have unlocked.
[/list][h3]🐞 Bug Fixes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] I’ve squashed several bugs, including terrain holes, UI layout issues, and tooltip glitches. Plus, improvements to signal placement and locomotive replacement ensure smoother gameplay.
[/list][h3]⚙️ Engine Update:[/h3]
[list]
[*] I’ve upgraded to Unity 6 LTS for better performance and to prepare for future enhancements.
[/list]
[h2]🗣️ Your Feedback Matters[/h2]
Your feedback is invaluable to me! I’m committed to listening to your suggestions and improving Train World based on what you share. Please keep the feedback coming—I’m always looking for ways to make the game better for you.
[h2]🚆 Coming Soon: Train World Driver Beta[/h2]
I’m also excited to announce that the Train World Driver Beta is just around the corner! Stay tuned for more information on how you can get involved and experience the next evolution of Train World.

Thank you for your continued support and passion for Train World. Let’s keep building something amazing together!

Happy railroading!

notes.title: Biomes update, new content
notes.notes:
The biomes and vegetation update cycle begins. I've updated the data structure and increased the number of biomes represented in the game. At this time changes will be minor. This first step will allow me to introduce new trees and vegetation to the biomes without map updates. Older maps will be updated with time and their appearance may change significantly. All of this will not influence previous save files. These changes will be purely visual. 

New trains were added in today's update:
[list]
[*] J Class is a powerful steam locomotive that bridges the gap between Big Boy and less powerful steam locomotives in the second era
[*] NRE 3GS is a diesel locomotive with moderate power that will be very useful in the late game for routes that do not have a lot of cargo capacity 
[*] ACS 64 is a powerful electric locomotive that has been requested for some time now and will be equally useful for passenger and freight operations
[*]  Avelia Liberty will be the pinnacle of the US train tree. With a maximum speed of 350 km/h, this train brings the US into the era of high-speed trains 
[/list]
Today's update also has one new map. Aurelia Atoll has an exciting donut-like shape with 2 ports. I hope this will be a welcome addition, especially for people who like to play on the smaller maps. 

In recent weeks, I focused on quality-of-life features, improvements to existing functionality, bug fixes, and adding requested features. 

Here is a list of some of the changes:
[list]
[*] Reputation reworked
[*] Updated signals placement logic
[*] Replace panel wagon/locomotive selection logic updated
[*] Improved parallel rail construction
[*] Improved Load panel opening speed
[*] Improved Load panel opening speed
[*] New Game UI reworked
[*] Alco PA/PB locomotives were replaced with EMD F7 A/B
[*] Added ability to assign color groups to trains
[*] Added floating text on maintenance and delivery payments
[*] Follow camera movement logic updated
[*] A lot of bug fixes
[/list]
As for the future, I’ll continue working on biome updates, address train placement quirks (trains jump sometimes), and implement new features and content

Thank you for your interest in the project and your support.

notes.title: Big update arrived
notes.notes:
I am happy to say that the Big update is here. In my previous announcements, I already shared some information on the changes. Here is the last part.

Reputation:
[list]
[*] Calculated each time the train delivers cargo. Train utilization and connection utilization are taken into account
[*] Reputation controls how many research points a player gets
[*] Low reputation will block loans or the unlocking of new regions
[/list]
Achievements:
[list]
[*] In-game achievements are almost the same as Steam achievements, but they are unique for each session and provide an additional income stream
[*]  Achievements are useful, especially during the early stages when cash is low
[/list]
Trains inventory:
[list]
[*] Added inventory allows a player to keep locomotives and wagons for future use
[*] This is very handy for completing one-time contracts as a player does not need to sell the train or wagons after use
[*] Locomotives in inventory do not lose lifespan or pay maintenance
[/list]
Industries:
[list]
[*] More than 32 industries
[*] Production becomes available over time and may be different based on what resources are available at the moment
[*] Some industries have production only in the late era (cars, tractors, etc.)
[*] Production may require up to 5 different components
[*] More than 160 cargo types are available now
[/list]
Depots:
[list]
[*] Can be placed anywhere
[*] Can be selected as a waypoint. In this case, the route becomes linear and will terminate at the depot. Very useful for one-time contracts
[*] When launching a train, the train will always go to the first waypoint in the route
[/list]
Visuals:
[list]
[*] Added new vegetation and animal models
[*] Added 2 new wagons
[*] Added models for new cargo types
[/list]
What's next? 
[list]
[*] Fixing any issues that may be discovered. 
[*] Continue to work on train navigation and movement, quite a bit still needs to be done there. 
[*] Additional research on the economy model is required and more updates will be in that department. A lot was changed in the current update and things got better, but there is still room to improve. 
[*] The help section needs more work
[*] Visuals and graphics updates needed
[/list]

On a larger scale: more content, locomotives, wagons, maps, and more diversity in biomes. I will start a new round of feedback collection to make a new plan for the next big update. 

Thank you for your support and interest in the project.

notes.title: Development update
notes.notes:
Hi, I want to give an update on the development process for the upcoming big changes to the game. I want to give a high-level 
 overview of what is in the works and also what is planned to be added in the update. Note, that all of the things below are current state descriptions and are subject to change

Transport logic:
[list]
[*]Passengers and freight are constantly transported by other means. The train transport now competes with these other means. So, no more situations when the production is not operating because one of the components is not delivered
[/list]

Economy:
[list]
[*]Passengers are separated into two categories: local and regional. Local passengers want to travel to the neighboring cities. Regional passengers want to travel between neighboring capitals 
[*]The player is able to set a price level per connection. This influences the number of passengers generated by the connection. The relationship is not linear so it allows for various strategies in passenger transport
[*]Freight transport is also split into two categories: one-time contracts and recurring deliveries. One-time contracts pay a fixed sum of money for a specific cargo delivered to the neighboring capital. Recurring requires a constant flow of cargo from the source to the destination. Recurring deliveries are split into batches. A player is able to adjust batch sizes that will be transported
[*]Transportation profits were significantly reworked. Now profits are calculated from actual spending (maintenance and train cost) and a set margin 
[/list]

Maps and industries:
[list]
[*]Maps will be significantly updated, and regions will be changed. Expect city density closer to the one seen in the "Noran Island" map.  The number of cities per region is reduced to four including the capital. So "Noran Isand" will have five regions
[*]Each region will have industry specialization with production centered around that specialization
[*]Regions do not have default consumption. This was replaced by industry-centered deliveries and one-time contracts
[*]Production facilities appear on the map as the player progresses with the game and the type of facilities that appear is random and depends on available resources
[*]The plan is to have over twenty industry specializations with more than a hundred production facilities and cargo types
[/list]

Trains:
[list]
[*]Trains are split into passenger and freight. Passenger trains will never be able to become freight trains and vice versa
[*]Lines were removed, and now trains have routes that a set per train. While cloning a train a player has an option to include the route
[*]Depots were added. Now the train has to get to the route from the closest depo
[*]Routes can end at the depot. This way the route will not be looped (very useful for one-time contracts)
[*]Cargo types are grouped (liquid, bulk, etc.). Now wagons and stations transport specific groups
[*]Added locomotives lifespan. When the train reaches the end of its lifespan the power drops significantly to the point that the train stops.  Lifespan affects sell price
[*]Added adjustable maintenance. Higher maintenance will cost more, but expend lifespan of the locomotive
[*]A few wagons will be added
[/list]

UI:
[list]
[*]Will reflect all the changes as well as some minor updates and improvements
[/list]

I will provide information on other changes in the next announcements. I hope you will like the changes. 

Important, previous saves will not be compatible with the new version. I will try to keep the old version of the game available on a separate branch.

notes.title: Major Demo Update
notes.notes:
Hi, finally, I can present you our big demo update.  

I am also happy to say that we are moving closer to the point where we will be able to release the game. I hope to make a release date announcement very soon. 

Here is a list of what was introduced and changed in a recent update:
[list]
[*] Updated signals mechanic. Now signals can be used as waypoints.
[*] Added "No stop" mechanic. Signal blocks train from stopping on a certain section of tracks. 
[*] Signals icons on the map represent the current signal state and switch accordingly
[*] Added station parameters: loading, unloading, wait time, etc.
[*] Added expandable freight station that can serve all types of wagons. 
[*] Updated passenger generation.
[*] Updated economy, added useful data about trains to the economy window (wait time, utilization)
[*] Updated UI (icons, cursors, UI fixes)
[*] Added "Bulk replace" mechanic, that allows replacement of a certain wagon or a locomotive
[*] Maps updated. A dedicated tutorial map was added.
[*] Improved rail construction. 
[*] Added an ability to view track usage, track direction, and signal states in a special construction overlay.
[*] Train block error now contains the name of the train that is blocking the path.
[*] Updated graphics and color scheme.
[*] A lot of bug fixes and quality improvements. 
[/list]
Also, a lot of work was made on the systems that are not present in the Demo. 

Unfortunately, old save files will not work with the new update.

notes.title: Signals update and future development
notes.notes:
Hi, here is a list of what was added and changed in a recent update:
[list]
[*] Added icons for signals to the map
[*] Added icons for the disconnected rail segments
[*] Updated signal placement and edit
[*] Updated signal panel
on the remove button on the signal panel
[*] Added button for switching construction view
[*] Added rail direction/usage lines
[/list]
[i]To edit the signal[/i]: click on it to select and then click again to change the direction or click on the button on the signals panel.

[i]To remove the signal[/i]: click on the signal icon to select it and then "[i]Left Click + Right Ctrl[/i]" or click 

Lines on top of the rails display which direction the trains can go. Green line - the rail track is not occupied and the red line - the rail track is occupied

[i]Known issue: in some occasions, signals may not load correctly from the save file. This will be fixed after the next big update.[/i] 

It will take a while for the next update. I am planning to have a lot of major changes. The majority of those changes will be under the hood and will not affect gameplay. Unfortunately, the next big update will not be compatible with the current saved files. I hope this will be the only time I have to break persistence between saved files.

notes.title: Regular update.
notes.notes:
Hi, Train World Fans!

I am happy to present an interactive tutorial step-by-step for Train World. I got a lot of feedback that it is a challenge for newcomers to start playing and I wanted to make sure that there is a tool for new players to learn how to play the game.

Based on your feedback, I've updated the camera controls and expanded camera rotation angles. The train 'Follow camera' got a major update and now can be positioned with more freedom. 

You can now switch off the UI by pressing the 'K' key on the keyboard. This will be useful for making screenshots and videos. 

Thank you for your support and feedback!
